name: Cessna 208 Caravan
summary: Single-engine utility turboprop used for FedEx Feeder cargo, commuter, skydiving and floatplane work.

wings: High-mounted, strut-braced straight wing with one strut per side
engines: Single PT6A turboprop in a long nose, usually with a three-blade prop
Exhaust stack on the right side of the cowling
fuselage: Long, boxy fuselage with rectangular windows
Fixed tricycle gear with spring-steel main legs
Often a large cargo pod under the belly; some on amphibious floats
tail: Conventional low tail with a tall swept fin and dorsal fillet

tellTales: Single turboprop with a strut-braced high wing on a long boxy body
Large cargo pod slung under the belly

confusedWith.howToTell: The Caravan is longer and lower-slung with a boxy body; the Kodiak is shorter and stubbier on taller gear with a tall fin.
The Caravan is much larger with a turboprop nose and tricycle gear plus often a belly pod; the 206 is a small piston single.
The Caravan has a strut-braced high wing and fixed gear; the PC-12 has a low wing, retractable gear and a T-tail.
The SkyCourier is a twin with a T-tail and a deeper, wider fuselage; the Caravan is a smaller single with a low tail.
The 750XL is a boxier, slab-sided aircraft with no pod; the Caravan has a rounder, tapered body and often a cargo pod under the belly.
The Porter is a tailwheel aircraft with a long, tapering nose; the Caravan has fixed tricycle gear.
